prompt: Company profile: Metal stamping plant in Kenosha, Wisconsin; 150 employees. Situation: A new high-tonnage press line was commissioned. Area noise monitoring in the press bay shows employee full-shift exposures around 88 dBA TWA; the rest of the plant is below 80 dBA. About 25 employees work in the press bay. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
### Compliance Obligations Register: Metal Stamping Plant – Press Bay Noise Exposure

**Company Profile:** 150-employee metal stamping facility in Kenosha, WI. New high-tonnage press line commissioning resulted in 25 employees with full-shift noise exposures of **88 dBA TWA** (press bay). Remainder of plant <80 dBA.

---

#### **Obligation 1: Hearing Conservation Program Implementation**
- **Requirement:** Establish and maintain a hearing conservation program for all employees exposed at or above the 85 dBA TWA action level. Program must include: noise monitoring, audiometric testing, hearing protection, training, and recordkeeping.
- **Source:** 29 CFR 1910.95(c)-(o); Wisconsin Admin. Code **SPS 332.04** (Wisconsin Occupational Noise Exposure Standard)
- **Applicability:** Directly applies to 25 press bay employees at 88 dBA TWA. State plan state—Wisconsin DSPS enforcement.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal & other requirements)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Audit program documentation, inspect hearing protection use, review audiometric test results, interview employees, verify training records.  
  - **When:** Initial compliance assessment within **30 days** of monitoring results; thereafter **annually** and whenever process/equipment changes occur. Conduct quarterly spot audits of critical elements (PPE use, signage).

---

#### **Obligation 2: Engineering & Administrative Control Evaluation**
- **Requirement:** Assess feasibility of engineering/administrative controls to reduce noise exposure. While not mandatory below 90 dBA PEL, Wisconsin’s “as low as reasonably achievable” (ALARA) principle under SPS 332.10 requires good-faith effort to reduce exposures >85 dBA.
- **Source:** 29 CFR 1910.95(b)(1); Wisconsin Admin. Code **SPS 332.10**
- **Applicability:** Required for new press line; must evaluate enclosure, isolation, or dampening options to mitigate 88 dBA exposure.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal & other requirements)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Documented feasibility study by qualified industrial hygienist; cost-benefit analysis; review of vendor noise specs for future purchases.  
  - **When:** Within **90 days** of commissioning; re-evaluate **annually** or when new technology becomes available.

---

#### **Obligation 3: Hearing Protection Provision & Enforcement**
- **Requirement:** Provide NRR-rated hearing protectors that reduce exposure to below 85 dBA (minimum 50% attenuation), ensure proper fit, and enforce use for all exposed employees.
- **Source:** 29 CFR 1910.95(i); Wisconsin Admin. Code **SPS 332.14**
- **Applicability:** Mandatory for 25 press bay employees; must post signage and enforce use in designated high-noise zones.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal & other requirements)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Monthly PPE inspections, annual fit-testing (quantitative or qualitative), review of attenuation calculations, audit enforcement protocols.  
  - **When:** Fit-testing **annually**; field compliance checks **monthly**; attenuation verification **semi-annually**.

---

#### **Obligation 4: Audiometric Testing Program**
- **Requirement:** Establish baseline and annual audiometric testing; provide testing within 6 months of initial exposure and annually thereafter. Track Standard Threshold Shifts (STS).
- **Source:** 29 CFR 1910.95(g); Wisconsin Admin. Code **SPS 332.12**
- **Applicability:** All 25 press bay employees; must use Wisconsin-certified audiometric facility or mobile unit.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal & other requirements)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Review audiometric technician certifications, STS follow-up documentation, referral logs, quality control checks of test environment.  
  - **When:** Baseline within **6 months** of assignment; **annually** thereafter; review STS cases within **30 days** of identification.

---

#### **Obligation 5: Employee Training & Information**
- **Requirement:** Annual training on health effects of noise, hearing protector fitting/use, and purpose of audiometric testing. Training must be understandable.
- **Source:** 29 CFR 1910.95(k); Wisconsin Admin. Code **SPS 332.16**
- **Applicability:** 25 press bay employees; must be completed before initial assignment and annually.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal & other requirements)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Review training records, conduct post-training assessments (quizzes), interview employees for comprehension, audit training content against standard.  
  - **When:** Upon initial assignment and **annually**; evaluate effectiveness **quarterly** via employee feedback.

---

#### **Obligation 6: Noise Exposure Monitoring & Recordkeeping**
- **Requirement:** Conduct initial and periodic noise monitoring; maintain exposure records for 2 years and audiometric records for duration of employment plus 30 years.
- **Source:** 29 CFR 1910.95(d) & (m); Wisconsin Admin. Code **SPS 332.06 & .18**
- **Applicability:** All monitoring data for press bay; new press line triggered initial monitoring requirement.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal & other requirements)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Audit calibration records of sound level meters/dosimeters, verify sampling methodology per OSHA Tech Manual, inspect record retention.  
  - **When:** Re-monitoring **annually** or after any equipment/process change; records audit **semi-annually**.

---

#### **Obligation 7: Community Noise (Environmental)**
- **Requirement:** If press bay noise impacts property line or community (e.g., outdoor loading, ventilation), comply with local noise ordinances.
- **Source:** **Kenosha Municipal Code Ch. 6.28** (Noise Control); Wisconsin Admin. Code **NR 190** (Industrial Noise)
- **Applicability:** Conditional—only if exterior noise levels exceed 55 dBA (residential) or 70 dBA (industrial) at property line. Requires assessment.
- **ISO 14001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Compliance obligations)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Conduct boundary noise survey per NR 190; review complaint logs; inspect mitigation measures.  
  - **When:** Initial assessment **within 60 days** of commissioning; **annually** or upon neighbor complaint.

---

### Summary Compliance Evaluation Schedule (ISO 9.1.2)

| Element | Frequency | Method | Responsible Party |
|---------|-----------|--------|-----------------|
| Hearing Conservation Program Audit | Annual | Full program review | EHS Manager |
| Engineering Controls Feasibility | Annual | Industrial hygiene study | Qualified Consultant |
| PPE Compliance | Monthly | Field inspections | Supervisors |
| Audiometric Testing Review | Annual + STS events | Audiometric data analysis | Occupational Health Provider |
| Training Effectiveness | Quarterly | Records & interviews | HR/EHS |
| Noise Monitoring | Annual or change-triggered | Dosimetry/sound mapping | Certified Industrial Hygienist |
| Community Noise | Annual or complaint-triggered | Boundary monitoring | EHS Manager |

**Note:** Wisconsin’s state-plan status means DSPS inspectors may enforce standards identically to OSHA but with state-specific reporting requirements. All obligations must be documented in the organization’s legal register and risk register under “Physical Hazards – Noise.”
